upload_failure.title: Wolta data upload failure
upload_failure.description: Wolta has been unable to upload energy data for more than 7 days. Last error: {error}. Check your internet connection and verify the integration is configured correctly.

profile_full.title: Wolta profile is full
profile_full.description: Your Wolta profile has reached its storage limit (about 2.3 years of 15-minute data), so new energy data can no longer be uploaded. Your grade and economy figures keep working on the stored history. To start fresh, remove the integration and set it up again.

flex_compensation_no_statistics.title: Wolta is not receiving your flex compensation
flex_compensation_no_statistics.description:
Nothing has reached Wolta from the sensor you picked for flex compensation ({entity_id}) — either it produced no monthly totals, or Wolta refused the amounts it did produce.

The most common cause is the sensor's `state_class`. Wolta reads the monthly sum from long-term statistics, which only exists for `state_class: total` or `total_increasing` — a `measurement` sensor does get long-term statistics, but only min/mean/max, and no monthly total can be read from it. A monthly total that comes out negative is skipped as well — Wolta only stores compensation of zero or more.

Pick a different sensor under Reconfigure, or leave the field empty to turn the feature off. Amounts you entered yourself on wolta.se are unaffected either way.

energy_stream_no_statistics.title: Wolta is not receiving data from one of your energy sensors
energy_stream_no_statistics.description:
One or more of the sensors you picked have stopped delivering statistics, or never delivered any ({streams}), while the upload window should have held data.

The most common cause is the sensor's `state_class`. Wolta reads energy deltas from statistics, which only carry them for `state_class: total` or `total_increasing` — a power sensor (W, `state_class: measurement`) produces statistics too, but without the sum column the deltas are read from, so the stream yields nothing at all. Wolta only sends quarters in which every selected sensor has a value of its own, so nothing is uploaded until the stream reads data again.

Pick the corresponding energy (kWh) sensor under Reconfigure. This warning clears itself as soon as the stream reads data again.

statistics_missing.title: Wolta has stopped uploading: a selected sensor has no statistics
statistics_missing.description:
{entities} has stopped producing statistics that Wolta can use, while your other selected sensors still do. Wolta only sends quarters in which every selected sensor has a value of its own, so uploading is paused until the sensor reports statistics again. The quarters from the paused period may not be sent afterwards.

Check that the sensor exists and is available in Home Assistant, and check its `state_class`: a power sensor (W, `state_class: measurement`) produces statistics without the sum column Wolta reads energy from, which counts as no statistics. If the sensor has been replaced by another one, select the new one under Reconfigure, or remove the old one there. If you pick a replacement, Wolta replaces the values of that sensor's energy stream (for example solar) in the history it already stores, from the statistics of the sensors now selected for the stream. The other streams' values are kept, except in short stretches (up to six hours) where the new sensors have no data: those quarters are removed. If you only remove the sensor, the stored history is left as it is. This warning clears itself once the sensor reports data again.

upload_stalled.title: Wolta has stopped uploading: no selected sensor gives new statistics
upload_stalled.description:
None of your selected energy sensors ({entities}) has given new statistics since {since}. Wolta only sends quarters in which every selected sensor has a value of its own, so nothing has been uploaded since then.

The most common cause is that the integration providing the sensors (often the inverter's or the battery's) has stopped working, or that the sensors are unavailable: check them under Settings → Devices & services. If the sensors have been replaced by new ones, pick the new ones under Reconfigure. A stopped Home Assistant recorder has the same effect. The time without statistics cannot be measured afterwards: the quarters from the stop are not sent. This warning clears itself as soon as the sensors give statistics again.

replacement_waiting_direction.title: Wolta: the battery direction change is waiting
replacement_waiting_direction.description: Wolta's server has temporarily stopped accepting corrections of the stored history for this plant, so the changed battery direction has not been applied to the stored history yet. The correction is retried automatically at {retry_at}. You don't need to do anything: new data is uploaded as usual, and this warning clears itself once the correction has gone through.

replacement_waiting_entities.title: Wolta: the sensor change is waiting
replacement_waiting_entities.description: Wolta's server has temporarily stopped accepting corrections of the stored history for this plant, so the values from the sensors you changed have not replaced the stored ones yet. The correction is retried automatically at {retry_at}. You don't need to do anything: new data is uploaded as usual, and this warning clears itself once the correction has gone through.

measured_capacity.title: Wolta measured a different battery capacity

init.title: Adopt the measured battery capacity?
init.description:
Over {days} days, Wolta measured your battery's usable capacity as about {measured} kWh, but your configuration works out to about {configured} kWh.

The measurement comes from your battery's own sensors (the ones you selected), not the electricity meter, and shows what the battery actually moves — not the rated/nameplate figure. Adopt it (this also clears any reserve, which the measurement already excludes), or keep your value — for example if you simply haven't fully cycled the battery in this period.

confirm.title: Adopt the measured battery capacity?
confirm.description:
Over {days} days, Wolta measured your battery's usable capacity as about {measured} kWh, but your configuration works out to about {configured} kWh.

The measurement comes from your battery's own sensors and shows what the battery actually moves — not the rated/nameplate figure. If those sensors measure on the AC side, it is also lower than the cell figure your battery app may show at 100 %, because the inverter loses energy converting to and from the battery. The grade compares you against a perfect controller on your hardware, so this value should match what the battery really moves.

Adopt {measured} kWh? This sets the battery capacity and clears any reserve (the measured value already excludes it). If you simply haven't fully charged or discharged in this period, you can ignore this and dismiss the issue.

init.title: Check your battery's maximum power
init.description:
Over {days} days, the most power your battery's own sensors have seen it charge or discharge is about {measured} kW, but you configured {configured} kW.

This is only what the battery has been *seen* doing, and a chronically spiky sensor can push it above what the hardware can really deliver. Set your battery's true maximum power (its inverter limit), or ignore this and keep the value you entered.

set_power.title: Set the battery's maximum power
set_power.description:
Over {days} days, the most power your battery's own sensors have seen it charge or discharge is about {measured} kW, but you configured {configured} kW.

This is only what the battery has been *seen* doing — if your control never demanded full power, the real maximum may be higher. Enter your battery's true maximum power (its inverter limit). A perfect controller would use all of it, so a value set too low would flatter your grade and one set too high would unfairly lower it. It's probably around {measured} kW — raise it if your battery can do more.

data_description.battery_kw: The battery's real maximum charge/discharge power (inverter limit), as its own sensors measure it. Pre-filled with the measured peak — adjust it if you know the battery can do more.

measured_efficiency.title: Wolta measured a different round-trip efficiency

init.title: Adopt the measured efficiency?
init.description:
Over {days} days, Wolta measured your battery's round-trip efficiency (energy out ÷ energy in, from the battery's own sensors) as about {measured}, but you configured {configured}.

Where those sensors measure depends on the installation: on a hybrid inverter often on the battery's DC side, on an AC-coupled battery on the AC side, which includes the inverter's losses. Adopt it to make your economics honest, or keep your value if you believe your real round-trip is higher — a spiky sensor can drag the measurement down.

confirm.title: Adopt the measured efficiency?
confirm.description:
Over {days} days, Wolta measured your battery's round-trip efficiency (energy out ÷ energy in, from the battery's own sensors) as about {measured}, but you configured {configured}.

The grade compares you against a perfect controller on your hardware, so the efficiency should match your battery's real round-trip where its sensors measure. This can drift when it was set from thin history at setup. Adopt {measured}?

Enter the manufacturer's figures – Wolta works out the usable capacity itself and switches to the measured value once the data allows.

house_copies.title: The same metering data exists in other plants at Wolta

confirm.title: Remove the copies?
confirm.description:
Uploads at Wolta with the same metering data as this plant ({count}), by upload day and data period:

{list}

They are counted once in the comparison with other houses. If you remove them they leave the comparison at once and are deleted after {days} days, unless someone holding their personal link chooses to keep them.

Until then, undo is on wolta.se: link the plant to an account (Configure → Link to a wolta.se account) and open it under My account.

grid_fee_implausible.title: Wolta: your grid fee looks too high
grid_fee_implausible.description:
The grid fee you entered is above {limit} öre (or cents) per kWh, higher than any variable grid fee we have seen. It most likely includes VAT and energy tax. Wolta adds both itself, so the energy tax is now counted twice, in the grade and in the economics.

Enter only the transfer fee, excluding VAT and energy tax, under Settings → Devices & services → Wolta → Configure → Settings → Tariffs. If your network operator really charges this much, you can leave it as it is.

grid_fixed_missing.title: Wolta: your grid fee needs its fixed part
grid_fixed_missing.description:
Your grid fee is entered as a percentage of the spot price, but without a fixed part. Wolta cannot work out what you pay for electricity without it, so the purchase-price sensor has no price (its state is unknown, see its reason attribute).

Enter the fixed part of your grid fee (the transfer fee, excluding VAT and energy tax) under Settings → Devices & services → Wolta → Configure → Settings → Tariffs. Enter 0 if you only have a percentage.

export_split_unclear.title: Wolta: separate your grid benefit from your retailer's terms
export_split_unclear.description:
You entered {export_extra} öre as export premium, and Wolta currently adds 5 öre of grid benefit on top. If {export_extra} is your grid benefit it is counted twice. Enter the grid benefit from your network operator and your retailer's terms separately, under Settings → Devices & services → Wolta → Configure → Settings → Tariffs.

Nothing changes until you save. Enter 0 as the retailer's terms if your retailer pays plain spot.

grid_benefit_fixed_missing.title: Wolta: your grid benefit percentage needs its fixed part
grid_benefit_fixed_missing.description: You entered {export_pct} % of spot as your grid benefit percentage, but not the fixed part of the grid benefit. Wolta then adds a standard 5 öre as the fixed part, which looks like your figure but is a guess. Enter the fixed part of your grid benefit (excluding VAT) under Settings → Devices & services → Wolta → Configure → Settings → Tariffs. Enter 0 if you only have a percentage.

soc_required.title: Wolta needs your battery's state-of-charge sensor

init.title: Your battery's state of charge
init.description:
Wolta needs the battery's state of charge (SoC, the charge level in %) so that the grade can be compared with other plants. Without it the grade is computed on the battery details you entered and is not compared.

If you pick a sensor, up to 365 days of its history is uploaded right away.

If the battery has no SoC sensor, say so. Plants that have neither picked a SoC sensor nor said that the battery has none will stop being able to upload data in a coming version.

energy_balance_solar_low.title: Wolta: your solar sensor probably reads too low
energy_balance_solar_low.description:
For a large part of your data, the battery takes in more energy than solar and grid import deliver in the same interval, so the sensors don't describe the whole house. Your grade is still shown to you, but it is kept out of the comparison with other installations.

It happens mostly while the sun produces, so your solar sensor ({solar}) probably reads too low. If the battery sits on the DC side of your inverter, the solar sensor must show solar production before the battery (the inverter's DC input), not the inverter's AC output. If you have several inverters or strings, all of them must be included.

Change the sensor under Reconfigure. This warning clears itself once Wolta's grading window no longer contains the mismatched data.

energy_balance_import_low.title: Wolta: your grid import or charge sensor doesn't add up
energy_balance_import_low.description:
For a large part of your data, the battery takes in more energy than solar and grid import deliver in the same interval, so the sensors don't describe the whole house. Your grade is still shown to you, but it is kept out of the comparison with other installations.

It happens mostly when you buy electricity from the grid, for example when charging at night. Check that the grid import sensor ({grid_in}) measures the whole installation's import (all phases) and that the charge sensor ({batt_in}) is the battery's own counter for charged energy.

Change the sensor under Reconfigure. This warning clears itself once Wolta's grading window no longer contains the mismatched data.

energy_balance_source_missing.title: Wolta: a solar or grid sensor seems to be missing
energy_balance_source_missing.description:
For a large part of your data, the battery takes in more energy than solar and grid import deliver in the same interval, so the sensors don't describe the whole house. Your grade is still shown to you, but it is kept out of the comparison with other installations.

The battery charges while neither solar nor grid import shows any energy. A sensor is probably missing from the configuration - check that both solar ({solar}) and grid import ({grid_in}) are selected.

Change the sensor under Reconfigure. This warning clears itself once Wolta's grading window no longer contains the mismatched data.

energy_balance_unclear.title: Wolta: your energy data doesn't add up
energy_balance_unclear.description:
For a large part of your data, the battery takes in more energy than solar and grid import deliver in the same interval, so the sensors don't describe the whole house. Your grade is still shown to you, but it is kept out of the comparison with other installations.

Check that solar ({solar}), grid import ({grid_in}), export and the battery's charge ({batt_in}) and discharge are mapped to the right sensors.

Change the sensor under Reconfigure. This warning clears itself once Wolta's grading window no longer contains the mismatched data.

battery_direction_all.title: Wolta: charging and discharging look swapped

init.title: Wolta: charging and discharging look swapped
init.description: When your data says the battery is charging, the battery's state of charge falls, and the other way round. This holds for all {reversed_days} days Wolta could check ({first_checked} – {last_reversed}). The charge ({batt_in}) and discharge ({batt_out}) sensors are probably swapped. Your grade is kept out of the comparison with other installations, and the economics use rule-of-thumb figures, until the direction is right.

Before that Wolta has no state of charge and cannot judge the direction. If the sensors ({batt_in}, {batt_out}) have been the same all along, you can flip the direction here. If you changed a sensor or a setting, correct what changed under Reconfigure instead. Your grade is kept out of the comparison with other installations, and the economics use rule-of-thumb figures, until the direction is right.

battery_direction_since.title: Wolta: charging and discharging became swapped
battery_direction_since.description: Since {since}, your data says the battery charges when its state of charge falls, and the other way round. Before that the direction was right. Something changed that day: a sensor, a setting or an update. Correct what changed. Do not flip the direction in Wolta's settings, since that flips the whole history and makes the time before {since} wrong. Once the direction is right again, let the grading window on wolta.se start after the correction. Your grade is kept out of the comparison with other installations, and the economics use rule-of-thumb figures, until the direction is right.

battery_direction_ended.title: Wolta: charging and discharging were swapped for a period
battery_direction_ended.description: Between {first_reversed} and {last_reversed}, charging and discharging were swapped in your data. After that the direction is right. Those days are still in your grading window. Let the window on wolta.se start after {last_reversed}, so the grade is only based on correct data. Your grade is kept out of the comparison with other installations, and the economics use rule-of-thumb figures, until the direction is right.

init.title: Wolta: charging and discharging became swapped
init.description: Since {since}, your data says the battery charges when its state of charge falls, and the other way round. Before that the direction was right. Something changed that day: a sensor, a setting or an update. Wolta can flip the direction for this period only: {swap_period}. The time before stays as it is, and nothing is re-sent. If you would rather correct what changed, do that instead of flipping here. Doing both makes the direction wrong again. Your grade is kept out of the comparison with other installations, and the economics use rule-of-thumb figures, until the direction is right.

entities.title: Select energy entities
entities.description: Select the energy sensors that measure your battery, grid and solar production. Battery and grid sensors are required; solar is optional.

data.soc_absent: My battery has no SoC sensor

data_description.external_control_entity: Sensor that is 'on' when the battery is controlled by a flex-market service (e.g. Tibber Grid Rewards). Those periods are counted neutrally in the optimisation grade.
data_description.flex_compensation_entity: Sensor holding the compensation your flex-market provider pays you (e.g. CheckWatt or Tibber Grid Rewards), in SEK. Wolta reads the monthly total and shows it next to what the flex participation cost you in foregone spot value. It must be a sensor with state_class total or total_increasing — a measurement sensor has no monthly sum to read. Amounts you have entered yourself on wolta.se are kept separately and are never overwritten.

user.title: Set up Wolta

menu_option_descriptions.create: Start from scratch – Home Assistant creates your Wolta profile.
menu_option_descriptions.link: Already used wolta.se? Paste your profile link or token and keep your existing history.

plant.title: Price zone and control system
plant.description: Battery capacity, power and efficiency are measured from your uploaded data – nothing to type. Your 15-minute energy data is stored at Wolta, your anonymised optimisation grade is included in the public comparison, and removing the integration deletes all of it. {zone_hint}

data_description.zone: Cannot be changed after the plant is created – it decides which price series your grade and economics are measured against.
data_description.control_system: Prefilled from your battery sensors' integration when Wolta recognises it – change it if it is wrong. Does not affect the grade; lets Wolta compare you with plants on the same system.
data_description.invert_battery: Turn on if your grade looks inverted (a strongly negative score). Preselected when your history shows more energy leaving the battery than entering it.

link.title: Link your wolta.se profile
link.description: Paste your personal wolta.se link (the one with ?profile=…) or just the token. Home Assistant takes over data uploads from here – overlapping periods are overwritten with sensor data.

invert_check.title: Check battery sensor direction
invert_check.description: Your history shows more energy leaving the battery than entering it, which usually means the charge/discharge sensors are swapped (common with signed meters like Shelly or Emaldo). Keeping this on uploads the streams swapped so your grade is computed correctly.

reconfigure.title: Change energy sensors
reconfigure.description: Pick the new sensors. Wolta replaces the changed sensors' values in the history it already stores, from the new sensors' statistics, and your grade is recomputed. Nothing else is re-sent, and there is no need to remove the integration.

data.soc_entities: Battery state of charge (%, one per battery)
data.soc_absent: My battery has no SoC sensor

data_description.external_control_entity: Sensor that is 'on' when the battery is controlled by a flex-market service (e.g. Tibber Grid Rewards). Those periods are counted neutrally in the optimisation grade.
data_description.flex_compensation_entity: Sensor holding the compensation your flex-market provider pays you (e.g. CheckWatt or Tibber Grid Rewards), in SEK. Wolta reads the monthly total and shows it next to what the flex participation cost you in foregone spot value. It must be a sensor with state_class total or total_increasing — a measurement sensor has no monthly sum to read. Amounts you have entered yourself on wolta.se are kept separately and are never overwritten.
data_description.soc_entities: Required for the grade to be compared with other plants. History of up to 365 days is uploaded right away. You can change the choice later under Reconfigure.

view_only.title: Add in view-only mode
view_only.description: This plant already streams its data to wolta.se through its own connection (Sonnen webhook or Reduxi), so Home Assistant will not upload anything to it. You get the Wolta sensors — grade, battery value, savings, IRR, payback — and the recompute button. Everything else is managed on wolta.se. Submit to add the plant in view-only mode.

reauth_new_token.title: New token for your plant
reauth_new_token.description: Your plant is linked to a wolta.se account, so Home Assistant needs a token from the account owner to reconnect. Log in on wolta.se, open the plant, choose Create new token and paste it here. Your history stays on the plant.

reauth_view_only.title: New token for view-only plant
reauth_view_only.description: The saved token no longer works — it was probably renewed on wolta.se. Paste a fresh profile link or token for the plant (log in on wolta.se and create one on the plant page). Nothing is created or changed on wolta.se.

abort.view_only_no_reconfigure: This plant is added in view-only mode and has no sensor selection to reconfigure. To start streaming from Home Assistant instead, remove this entry and link the profile again.

settings.title: Wolta profile
settings.description: These values are your shared Wolta profile – changes here show up on wolta.se too, and changes made on wolta.se show up here. Clear an optional field to remove its value.

data_description.battery_kwh: Usable capacity — the kWh the battery actually delivers on a full discharge, **as its own sensors measure it** – leave empty while Wolta is measuring. This is less than the nameplate rating. If the battery sensors measure on the AC side, it is also less than the energy your battery app shows at 100 % SoC (that's the DC/cell figure), because the inverter loses energy converting to and from the battery. The grade compares you against a perfect controller on YOUR hardware, so use the usable value — not nameplate — to keep the comparison fair. Batteries with a reserve/SoC floor (e.g. Emaldo) deliver even less. With a few months of history, Wolta measures this for you and can suggest the value via a Repair.
data_description.nameplate_kwh: The manufacturer-rated capacity (e.g. sonnen 10p/22 = 22 kWh nameplate / 20 kWh usable). Used by the expansion calculator on wolta.se so per-kWh prices (quoted per nameplate kWh) are compared fairly against what the battery actually delivers. Leave empty if your battery is marketed by usable capacity (e.g. Tesla Powerwall).
data_description.battery_kw: Maximum charge/discharge power in kW – leave empty while Wolta is measuring.
data_description.nameplate_kw: The manufacturer-rated power (e.g. 8 kW). The model uses the deliverable power above; the rated figure lets wolta.se explain the difference when the measured power is lower (e.g. inverter losses, derating). Leave empty if your battery is marketed by deliverable power.
data_description.eff: Round-trip efficiency (0.5–1.0) where your battery sensors measure: on a hybrid inverter often the battery's DC side, on an AC-coupled battery the AC side. Prefilled with the value stored at Wolta. Changing plant values triggers a server-side regrade.
data_description.reserve_pct: The share of usable capacity your control system never discharges below (e.g. backup reserve). The grade benchmark then plays with the same window you do. Enter usable capacity above — the reserve is subtracted here, don't subtract it twice. Clear the field to remove the reserve.

economy.name: Economy
economy.description: Entered a combined price for the whole plant (solar + battery) on wolta.se? Then the purchase price is managed there, and the price field is hidden here.

data.cost_sek: What you paid for the battery (kr) – battery only

data_description.cost_sek: What you actually paid for the BATTERY ONLY (not solar panels), in SEK — the invoice total, after any green deduction. Used to calculate the battery's IRR and payback. Clear the field to remove the value.
data_description.purchase_date: Date the battery (or solar+battery) system was installed. Used to calculate this year's actual savings. Date in the future (a planned purchase)? The results only show the actual outcome so far — for a planned purchase, use the decision calculator on wolta.se instead. Clear the field to remove the value.

tariffs.name: Tariffs
tariffs.description: Leave blank to use your country's standard tariff.

data.grid_benefit_ore: Grid benefit, rest of the year (öre per kWh)
data.grid_benefit_peak_ore: Grid benefit, high-load hours (optional, öre per kWh)
data.export_extra_ore: Retailer's terms for sold electricity (öre/ct per kWh)
data.grid_var_pct: Grid fee, percent of spot (% of spot)
data.export_extra_pct: Grid benefit, percent of spot (% of spot)

data_description.grid_var_ore: Your variable grid fee (transfer fee), excluding VAT and energy tax, in öre/kWh (SEK zones) or euro cents/kWh (other zones). Wolta adds VAT and energy tax itself. If your grid fee also has a percentage of spot (the field below), this is its fixed part and is required: enter 0 if you only have a percentage. Clear the field to revert to your country's standard tariff.
data_description.surcharge_ore: Your electricity supplier's markup, excluding VAT, in öre/kWh (SEK zones) or euro cents/kWh (other zones). Clear the field to revert to your country's standard tariff.
data_description.grid_benefit_ore: The grid benefit (nätnytta) your network operator pays per kWh you feed in, excluding VAT, in öre/kWh. It is on your network operator's statement and is not what your electricity retailer pays (that is the retailer's terms, below). Enter 0 if you get none. If it also has a percentage of spot (the percent field below), this is its fixed part and is required: enter 0 if you only have a percentage. Left empty, Wolta uses a standard 5 öre. Sweden (SE1–SE4) only, between −20 and 50. Clear the field to revert to the standard.
data_description.grid_benefit_peak_ore: Optional. The grid benefit for high-load hours, if your network operator pays a different amount then. Wolta counts weekdays 06–22 from November to March as high-load, except public holidays such as Christmas, New Year and Easter. It is an exception to the rest of the year, so that field is required too. Sweden (SE1–SE4) only, between −20 and 50. Clear the field to use the same amount all year.
data_description.export_extra_ore: What your electricity retailer pays (+) or deducts (−) per sold kWh, on top of the spot price, in öre/kWh. 0 if your retailer pays plain spot. This is not your grid benefit: enter that in the fields above, or it is counted twice. Can be negative. Clear the field to revert to your country's standard tariff.
data_description.grid_var_pct: The percentage part of your grid fee, as a percent of the spot price. It needs the fixed part in the field above (0 if you only have a percentage). Clear the field to remove the percent component.
data_description.export_extra_pct: The percentage part of your grid benefit, as a percent of the spot price (can be negative). It needs the fixed part in the rest-of-the-year field above (0 if you only have a percentage). Clear the field to remove the percent component.
data_description.reduced_energy_tax: Some municipalities in northern Sweden have a reduced energy tax: your grid operator deducts 9.6 öre/kWh excluding VAT on the bill. It applies in all municipalities in Norrbotten, Västerbotten and Jämtland, and in Sollefteå, Ånge, Örnsköldsvik, Ljusdal, Malung-Sälen, Mora, Orsa, Älvdalen and Torsby. Source: Skatteverket. Choose Yes if you live in one of them and No if you do not. Not set means you have not answered: in SE1–SE3 the purchase-price sensor has no price (its state is unknown) until you do.

data_description.invert_battery: Turn on if your grade looks inverted (a strongly negative score). Swaps battery charge and discharge for the whole history, so you don't have to change your Home Assistant sensors. Wolta corrects the data it already has; nothing is re-sent. Also shown as on when a repair flipped only part of the history. Turning it off restores the original direction everywhere.

account_link.title: Link to a wolta.se account
account_link.description:
Your linking code is **{code}**.

Go to wolta.se/konto, enter your email address and paste the code — if you do not have an account yet, one is created when you confirm the email. If you are already signed in, go to Account → Link plant instead. The code is valid for 10 minutes. Minting a new code invalidates any earlier one, even if it hasn't expired yet.

zone_correction.title: Correct the price zone
zone_correction.description: Change the electricity price zone if it was set wrong when this plant was created. The zone decides which prices your grade and economics are measured against, so correcting it recalculates them — your figures will change. Only zones in the same country are offered: the stored amounts are expressed in the zone's currency and are not converted.

error.battery_pair_incomplete: Capacity and power go together: fill in both, or leave both empty and let Wolta measure them.
error.grid_fixed_required: A grid fee given as a percentage of spot needs its fixed part too. Fill in "Grid fee" in the Tariffs section (0 if you only have a percentage).
error.grid_benefit_fixed_required: A grid benefit given as a percentage of spot needs its fixed part too. Fill in "Grid benefit, rest of the year" in the Tariffs section (0 if you only have a percentage).
error.grid_benefit_peak_requires_base: The high-load grid benefit is an exception to the rest of the year, so fill in "Grid benefit, rest of the year" too.
error.grid_benefit_zone: The grid benefit can only be given in price zones SE1–SE4, so it cannot be saved for this plant's zone.
error.cannot_connect: Failed to connect to Wolta API – check your internet connection and try again.
error.zone_rejected: Wolta rejected the correction. A zone can only be corrected within the same currency, and only by the plant's owner.

abort.cannot_connect: Could not reach wolta.se – profile editing needs a connection. Try again later.
abort.reauth_required: The profile no longer exists on wolta.se – re-authentication has been started, check your notifications.

recompute_failed.message: Wolta could not recompute right now – try again later
